could_not_run_reason: No paper target exists for this dataset: the paper reports computed numbers only for 5DK3 (RMSD) and 6UMT (binding free energies); 2XWT appears only as a Table 1 metadata row (5 seeds, 200 ns, footnote b). The production trajectory is not deposited, so no RMSD/RMSF/Rg/SASA/H-bond series can be regenerated. Only internal-consistency checks and pre-registered robustness checks on the deposited MMPBSA per-frame data were run.

internal_checks.term: GB dTOTAL recomputed with AmberTools 26 sander from deposited prmtop + mdcrd intermediates

robustness.description: Bootstrap of mean per-frame GB dTOTAL (20 frames), 10,000 resamples, default_rng(20261009); percentile 95% CI
robustness.note: No paper value exists for 2XWT; compared only with the deposited GB mean (-103.70): same sign, CI excludes 0. Not a different MD seed (only seed 3 deposited).

robustness.description: Drop frames with |z|>3 (ddof=1) on per-frame GB dTOTAL; if none, drop single lowest and highest frame
robustness.note: max |z| = 2.899, 0 frames with |z|>3, so fallback trim applied (dropped -122.02 and -70.82). No paper value.

robustness.description: Poisson-Boltzmann instead of Generalized Born: mean per-frame PB dTOTAL, same 20 frames
robustness.note: Sign differs from GB (-103.6975); same_sign_as_gb=False. Descriptive only; no paper value. Optional R_c2 (igb=2) not run.

bugs.description: Legend test l.startswith('@ s') also matches GROMACS '@ subtitle' lines, so the subtitle is taken as a column label and cut by split()[3:] and [1:-1].
bugs.evidence: 2xwt-rs3-310k-200ns-rmsd.xvg contains '@ subtitle "Protein after lsq fit to Protein"' and no '@ s0 legend' line; script header written: 'Time (ps),fter lsq fit to Protein'; Dataverse ingest variable names ['Time (ps)', 'fter lsq fit to Protein']. Same in 400 ns RMSD file. Label only; values unaffected.

bugs.description: First column label is hard-coded 'Time (ps)' regardless of the x axis of the .xvg file.
bugs.evidence: RMSD .xvg files were made with '-tu ns' and declare '@    xaxis  label "Time (ns)"', but the deposited CSV/.tab column is named 'Time (ps)' (values 0.0, 0.01, ... are ns). Units label wrong in deposited 200 ns and 400 ns RMSD .tab files.

bugs.description: Header row is written only when the number of '@ s' lines equals columns-1; for a .xvg with no legend lines (gmx rmsf) no header is written.
bugs.evidence: 2xwt-rs3-400ns-310k-rmsf.csv first line is '1,0.3080' (674 data rows); Dataverse ingest then used that row as variable names ['1', '0.3080'] and the ingested .tab has 673 cases, so residue 1 is missing from the ingested table (the original CSV still has it).

env_fixes: diffs/xvg2csv.py.diff: Python 2 print statements converted to print() calls so the script runs under Python 3.12 (no python2 interpreter available); no logic change.
class_reason: The deposit cannot reproduce any number reported in the paper: the paper reports no computed value for 2XWT, and the inputs needed to regenerate the 2XWT analyses (production .xtc trajectories) are not deposited. What can be run (the gmx_MMPBSA summary from its own per-frame data, and a sander GB rerun from the deposited intermediates) is internally consistent, but that is not a reproduction of the paper.
confidence_reason: Facts are checked by script, but C versus E (or 'not applicable') is a judgement because there is no paper target at all.
uncertainties: Class choice: PROTOCOL classes assume a paper number exists; C is chosen because the materials do not support any reported number. E would also be defensible only if one treats the missing trajectory as 'could not run'; we did run what exists.
PREREG asked for sample SD (ddof=1); the author SDs in FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat match population SD (ddof=0): GB dTOTAL SD ddof0 11.0520 vs ddof1 11.3391 vs author 11.05. Means are unaffected.
Images embedded in Supporting file 1 (12 images) and the main figures were not OCR'd; their text and captions do not mention 2XWT, and the main-text figures concern other PDB entries.

Table 1 lists 2XWT with 200 ns while the dataset title says 400 ns; 400 ns files are dated 2024-06-11 (after acceptance). The 400 ns RMSD series starts at about 4.48 nm at t=0 and contains a duplicated time point at 200 ns (40,002 rows), while the 200 ns series starts at 0.0005 nm; cause cannot be determined without the trajectories. Descriptive only, not a paper number.
AmberTools GB rerun from deposited intermediates: 20 frames, max per-frame |diff| vs deposited dTOTAL 0.0047 kcal/mol
Environment differs from the authors' (AmberTools 26 on aarch64 vs Amber 21 / gmx_MMPBSA 1.5.2 on x86_64).
